_comment: Copy this file to config.json and fill in your values.
_comment_windows: On Windows use full paths, e.g. C:\Program Files\Calibre2\calibredb.exe

ai._comment: Anthropic-only. Set api_key once here (or via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var). Per-command blocks only need a model — they inherit the top-level api_key. Add api_key to a per-command block only if you want a different key for that command.
ai._comment_models: Use a named alias ('fast', 'latest', 'legacy') or a literal Anthropic model ID. Aliases are resolved at startup against calibre_toolkit/models.py — when a new generation ships, only that file needs updating. Literal IDs continue to work.
ai._comment_retries: Anthropic client per-request timeout and number of retries on transient (429/5xx) errors. Built-in exponential backoff.

identifiers._comment_fetch: Leave blank to auto-detect from calibredb_path. On Windows set to e.g. C:\Program Files\Calibre2\fetch-ebook-metadata.exe
identifiers._comment_workers: Concurrent fetch-ebook-metadata calls during MQG-02. Each call is mostly network I/O so threading gives real speedup; 3–5 is a sane range. Drop to 1 to serialise.
identifiers._comment_sufficient: A book is considered already sufficient if it has at least one of these identifier types. Sufficient books skip the live lookup.
identifiers._comment_mqg_complete: Extra identifier types that must be present before MQG-02 is marked complete. Books enriched but missing these are reported as 'pending ratings' and not marked done. Set to [] to disable the gate.

fetcher._comment: fetch-ebook-metadata subprocess discipline. Overrides identifiers.lookup_timeout_seconds when present. max_retries applies only to transient failures (timeouts, network errors in stderr); missing-binary and no-results responses are not retried.

catalog._comment: LC catalog and Open Library HTTP discipline. max_retries applies to 5xx responses and connection failures; 4xx responses are treated as a definitive miss and not retried.

description._comment: MQG-03 book-description pre-fetch (Google Books -> Open Library). Falls back to `catalog` values when this block is absent. Graceful degradation: any miss leaves the AI to summarise from training data as before.
description._comment_google_books_api_key: OPTIONAL but strongly recommended. Without a key, only Open Library is queried — many books on it lack descriptions, so AI hallucination protection is weaker. Google Books has zero anonymous quota; every unauthenticated request returns HTTP 429. Setup (~3 min, free): see docs/Getting-Started.md section 'Step 2a — Google Books API key (optional)'. The env var GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY wins over this field if both are set.

lcc._comment: MQG-03 LCC enrichment — custom column labels (with leading #).

comments._comment: MQG-04 comments enrichment — custom column labels.

tags._comment: MQG-05 tag enrichment and review settings.

review._comment: Shared interactive-review settings. apply_confirm_threshold: when the user picks 'apply all' on a batch larger than this, ask one extra time before writing. Set to a very large number to disable.

usage._comment: Budget guardrail. Before a step's AI phase begins, the projected batch cost (from usage history, or a static estimate when history is thin) is compared against confirm_above_usd: above it, the run asks 'N books ≈ $X — proceed?' before any AI call. At or below it, no prompt. Dry-runs make real AI calls, so the gate fires on them too. Raise to a very large number to disable.
